summary.text: Michael Baumgartner is the Republican incumbent in Washington's 5th District, elected in 2024 to succeed Cathy McMorris Rodgers. A Pullman native with an economics degree from Washington State University and a Harvard master's in public administration, he worked as a State Department officer in Baghdad before serving eight years in the Washington State Senate and six years as Spokane County Treasurer.

paragraphs.text: Baumgartner was born in Pullman, Washington, in 1975. According to his campaign website, he grew up among the Palouse wheat fields in Colton and then Pullman, the son of two educators.

He earned a bachelor's degree in economics from Washington State University in 1999 and a Master of Public Administration in international development from Harvard University in 2002. His campaign website says he spent a year volunteering with the Jesuits in Africa before Harvard, where he was a Teaching Fellow in Economics.

After working in private business in the Middle East, he served as a U.S. State Department officer at the U.S. Embassy in Baghdad, Iraq, from 2007 to 2008, then as a counternarcotics advisor to a U.S. government-funded program in Afghanistan. He also worked as a part-time economic adviser to the U.S. military.
Baumgartner was the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Washington in 2012, according to his campaign website.

He served in the Washington State Senate representing the 6th Legislative District from 2011 to 2019. His campaign website says he played a lead role in creating a WSU medical school in Spokane, in funding the North-South Freeway, and in a reduction in college tuition, and that his "Drain the Swamp" legislation eliminated five state agencies.
He then served as Spokane County Treasurer from 2019 to 2025, overseeing a roughly $1.9 billion fixed-income investment fund.

Baumgartner was elected to the U.S. House in 2024 and took office in 2025. He serves on the Judiciary, Foreign Affairs, and Education and the Workforce committees, and his official site lists him as vice chair of the Education and the Workforce Subcommittee on Higher Education and Workforce Development, chairman of the College Sports Caucus, and vice chair of the Republican Policy Committee.
His official biography lists honors including the Washington Policy Center's "Champion of Freedom Award" and the Inland Empire Society of American Foresters' "Legislator of the Year" award.
According to his official biography, he lives in Spokane with his wife, Eleanor, and their five children.
